neighbours.label: a physical object being wrapped, inserted or gripped by hand (wrapped with cloth, loosen his grip, put into)
fire: She carefully wrapped the vase in old newspaper before packing it.
Gently loosen his fingers and take the scissors out of his hand.
The nurse wrapped the bandage tightly around the injured ankle.
He pushed the cork back into the bottle with his thumb.
Slide the key into the lock and turn it twice to the left.
The baker wrapped the dough in plastic and left it in the fridge.
She tucked the letter inside her coat pocket and hurried out.
The climber gripped the rope with both hands and pulled himself up.
quiet: She carefully chose the vase at the market before going home.
Gently remind him that the scissors belong in the drawer.
The nurse explained how long the injured ankle would take to heal.
He talked about the bottle of wine he had bought in France.
Remember the key code and tell it to the guard at the gate.
The baker sold the bread at the market and went home early.
She read the letter twice at the kitchen table and sighed.
The climber looked at the rope and decided to rest for a while.

notes: Card: wrapped x2, 'sc'rolled, his (grip), Chinese 进/它/行李 in put-into constructions; output promotes off/threads/board/hang/under.
